Every man is born corporeal, becomes sensuous, then natural, and successively rational; and if he does not then come to a stand, he becomes spiritual. The reason of this progression is in order that planes may be formed...
I once heard a voice from Heaven saying that if there were a spark of life in man... there would be no Heaven...
Unless the understanding could be perfected separately, and the will through it, man would not be man, but a beast. Explained. TCR 588:2.
The reason man is man is that his understanding can be elevated above the desires of his will...
That the Infinite is... in men as in its images. General article.
(Thus) man is an organ recipient of God...
In men the light of life, which is intelligence, and the heat of life, which is love, are divided... because man is to be reformed and regenerated...
That man was created a form of Divine order. General article.

As man is the principal end of creation, it follows that each and all things have been created for the sake of man, and consequently that each and all things of order have been collected into him, and concentrated in him, in order that through him God may effect primary uses.

That man is so far in power against evil and falsity from the Divine omnipotence, and that he is so far in wisdom concerning good and truth from the Divine omniscience, and that he is so far in God from the Divine omnipresence, as he lives according to Divine order. General article.
It is a general canon in Heaven that God is in every man, both evil and good; but that man is not in God unless he lives according to order...
II. That God created man from order, in order, and into order.
That thus God became man, and man God, in one Person. General article. TCR 102.
This arcanum: That the soul which is from the father is the man himself; and that the body which is from the mother is not the man in himself, but is from him...
From these things the Angels know that in the universal Spiritual World the Lord alone is a full man.
From himself man is merely passive; but through the influx of life from the Lord he is also active...
The Lord from Himself or from the Word acts in man; but not through him; because man acts and speaks freely from the Lord when from the Word.
The quality of man's Internal if he were not reformed by the Lord. Described.
That there are no ideas connate with men...
That the Lord inflows with all His Divine love, with all His Divine wisdom, thus with all His Divine life, with every man. General article.
That the things which inflow from the Lord are received by man according to his form. General article.
That the Lord is charity and faith in man, and that man is charity and faith in the Lord. General article.
Man has been created so that he can be conjoined with God...

There is no such reciprocal conjunction of the Lord with man; but there is mutual conjunction, which is not effected by means of actions and reactions, but by means of cooperations; for the Lord acts, and man receives the action from the Lord, and operates as of himself, nay, from himself from the Lord. This operation of man from the Lord is imputed to him as his...
That spurious faith... is with those who... regard the Lord... solely as a man. General article.
For there is with every man a consociate Spirit, because without this he cannot think analytically, rationally, and spiritually; thus would not be man but a brute...
That every man in the singular is the neighbour who is to be loved; but according to the quality of his good. General article.
Man is not born for the sake of himself, but for the sake of others; that is, that he should not live for himself alone, but for others...
That man in the plural, which is a society... and that man in the composite, which is our country, is the neighbour who is to be loved. General article.

When the Lord and an Angel look down into the earth, they see a whole society no otherwise than as one man... I too have been permitted to see a certain Society in Heaven exactly as one man, in like stature to that in which is man in the world.
Man is not man from the human face and body, but from his wisdom... and goodness... When man is born he is more a brute than any animal, but becomes a man through instructions...
That man is not life, but a receptacle of life from God. General article.
Man alone receives light and heat immediately from the Lord. This is the difference.
In the middle of this interspace is every man as to his spirit...
Through this the Lord inspires life into man which is distinct from the life of beasts.

As to charity and faith, the Lord acts, and man acts from the Lord; for there is the Active of the Lord in the Passive of man; and therefore the power to act well is from the Lord, and the derivative will to act is as of the man, because he is in free will... The action of man concordant with the action of the Lord is what is here meant by cooperation.
As (the heat of the Spiritual Sun) essentially breathes the generation of man, it induces a certain likeness of man on whatever it generates.
From birth man inclines to evils of every kind... and is a Hell in miniature. Described.

Hence it is that there are three things in man as to his Internal; namely, the soul or mind, the will, and the understanding. These three are receptacles of those universals; the soul or mind is the receptacle of the Lord... the will is the receptacle of love or good, and the understanding is the receptacle of wisdom or truth...

In like manner there are three things in man as to his External, to which also each and all things relate and on which they depend; to wit, the body, the heart, and the lungs. Moreover, these three things of the body correspond to the three things of the mind...
Every man is his own love and his own intelligence... Therefore all things which proceed from a man... make the man, and are the man himself.
In the greatest society, which is called the world, there are four kinds of men; the spiritual, the natural, the intermediate, and those who are opposite to these... WE 326. WE 327. WE 328. WE 330.
On the three general differences between men and Souls. SE 2019.
The quality of men when left to themselves...
How it is to be understood that man can do nothing with his Own strength...
How few men there would be even if there were thousands of worlds...
On the interiors of man.
That the universe corresponds to the things which are in man...
That men are worse than wild beasts.
That if man were in order he would enjoy every sense which brutes enjoy.
That every society is a man.
That Societies have their own Spirits near men.
Nothing else is required with man than to be a yielding vessel...
Every man is born into all evil...
(Thus) man can do nothing but evil...
That there can be no mercy, nor innocence, of man.
That the Lord has led the human race since the creation of the first man.
How could the first man have come forth... before the Grand Body was formed...
These genera, and these species of men had been unknown to me...
That the perceptive view and affection of ends distinguishes man from brutes.
That spiritual minds are men.
How the influx of Spirits is effected into man...
Man is continually wishing to precipitate himself into the worst evil.
That the Angels can know the whole nature of a man or Spirit from one of his ideas.

With man there are not such spheres, because he is in phantasies. Man too would not only have such spheres, which are the lowest, but would have a sphere of Knowing his companion as soon as he saw him...
These have their feet in man.
They who are recently arrived from the Earth from fallacy appear to themselves as men.
That which appears clear to man is obscure to good Spirits... Explained.
Therefore unless the Lord saw man to be something, the whole World of Spirits would see him as nothing...
That men are kept in a Society of Spirits.
That men are vessels.
It is the prerogative of man... that he can think of and view those things which are... spiritual and celestial, which beasts cannot do; and thus have as an end the Societies of the other life...
Men appear to Spirits as a black mass without life...
On the Spirits who are with man.
Man was created after the type of both worlds...

Wherefore it has been so provided by the Lord that the Divine shall pass through man from the Spiritual World into the natural world... and that thus through man there should be the connection of the Spiritual World with the natural world...
Such as a man is in his organic principles, such is he wholly...
There is an influx thence into every man; for his interiors are formed after the image of Heaven...
In the midst there was an obscure something, which was said to be the man around whom they are...
On the Hells around man.

The man who has not yet become actually evil appears above the earth there... but as it were veiled with a very dense and opaque membrane... Below he appears as an obscure and inanimate something. This appears to the Angels, but not to the Spirits who are there... But when he acquires a life of evil he is more and more submerged beneath the plane of the earth, first to the feet, afterwards to the loins, then to the breast, and finally to the head; and then he is in Hell, and he cannot be elevated thence, because he is then in adult and even old age, and can no longer receive new truths, nor can those which are with him be bent, because they have become hard. He then appears there, and at last much lower; and it was perceived that when a man is not far from the end of his life, his head droops, and at last his body bends forward...
When about to die, his head droops, and at last he falls.

The Divine Itself in its first essence was a man in endeavour, or in becoming, whence it was like a man; thus a man reflexively; and the second essence was a man born and essentially from the first; and the third essence was a man proceeding in what was successive, which is the whole Heaven...
Man is therefore as it were the plane upon which are the thoughts of the Angels...

There are four kinds of men there, as in the world. The first attend to the uses in the Word... they serve as a plane. Thus is it read by the celestial. The second are those who take the doctrinal things of the Word; thus do the spiritual apprehend it. The third are those who are delighted solely with its holy external, without intelligence; these are they who are in the ultimate Heaven. And the fourth are they who attend only to the literal sense; and they who attend solely to the words, as critics... the former are in the threshold of Heaven, and the latter are in the very extremes.
The natural thought of man is the plane in which cease all things of angelic wisdom...
The Angels... are not turned to themselves, but to men...

The plane and the ultimate is with an intelligent man, whether he is thinking about such things, or about other things, or is asleep... For the whole man is such as are the truth and good with him. Many men can simultaneously serve as one plane for one Angel. The Lord so disposes that what is absent in one may be in another...

That the spirit of man appears in the other life... But this takes place with those only who think within themselves more deeply... But those who think solely in their Sensuous... never appear. Nor do Spirits know anything about man, as to where he is... for if evil Spirits knew where a man is, and that they were with a man, they would utterly destroy him... They hold men as vile... But the Lord loves men. DMin 4693.
Those who remained appeared together as one man. Those who were outside him were cast out... SE 5769.
That Heaven relates to one man.
For the nature of every thing has been inscribed on man.
All were told that they are no longer men...
All (in the temples) when taken together form as it were one man...
That in the other life all who acknowledge the Divine think of God as a Man.
Concerning God as a Man. SE 6061.
A man who is rare () = those who are in truths.

Had a face like a man = the Divine... as to wisdom... (For) a man = one who receives Divine truth; and (therefore) by a man is signified wisdom; for man was created to be rational and wise... Hence it is that by man in the Word is signified wisdom. The reason man = the affection of truth and at the same time wisdom, is that (these two things) act as one. Some suppose that man is man from his face and body, and that he is by these distinguished from beasts. But they are in error. Man is man from wisdom; and therefore in the proportion that anyone is wise, in the same proportion is he a man; (and so appears in the other life).
That by man, in the Word, is signified the affection of truth, and the derivative wisdom. Illustrated. AE 315:6.
As man = the spiritual affection of truth and the derivative wisdom, he also = the Church. Illustrated.
But by man, in the supreme sense, is meant the Lord Himself. Explained, Illustrated.
Man = wisdom. AE 304:24. AE 370:2.
Two things make man... good and truth...
Man = intelligence and wisdom. AE 400:9.
Man, in the opposite sense, = the desire for falsity and the derivative insanity.
Before the Lord the Church in the whole world is as one man...
Man, here = intelligence from proprium...
Man and beast = spiritual affection and natural affection. AE 388:20.
Man is called man from the good of life.
A man = the reception of truth from spiritual affection and the derivative intelligence.
Man = intelligence.
Man is man according to the way in which the Knowledges with him live...
Man () = man as to wisdom; and the son of man = man as to intelligence.
Unless Jehovah had been for us when man rose up against us () = when man from himself, from his own love, and from his Own intelligence... endeavours to destroy the truths of the Church.
Man, in the Word, = the understanding of truth; and man, the perception of good.
Man = the affection of truth and the derivative intelligence and wisdom; here () the understanding of truth and the perception of good. Explained.
This faculty man never loses...
If he loses this faculty he is no longer man... It is from this that man lives after death...
Like the faces of men = like spiritual affections of truth.
All in the Heavens are men...
But in Hell... they appear among themselves as men...
Thy men shall fall by the sword () = that the understanding of truth will be destroyed through falsities.
By man () is meant the Church in general and in particular.
To hurt men five months () = to induce stupor on the understanding of truth and the perception of good so long as they are in that state.
To kill the third part of men () = to deprive themselves of all the understanding of truth and the derivative spiritual life. AE 579.
To sacrifice a man () = to destroy the spiritual life.
A man = Divine truth in light and intelligence.
He devoured men () = the destruction of all the understanding of truth. AE 722:2.
Under Beast, see this reference. AE 650:4. AE 650:15. AE 650:16. AE 650:18. AE 650:20. AE 650:21. AE 768:4. AE 1100:16.
Man () = the derivative intelligence.

For man as to his external or natural man is nothing but a beast... and therefore the natural man may be called the animal man. But the reason what is internal or spiritual is signified by man, is that man is man as to his Internal or Spiritual...
Man () = all these (thoughts, affections, etc.) from primes to ultimates.
Their derivative intelligence is signified by man.
That the natural man does not understand Divine things from himself, is signified by, Egypt is man, and not God.
I will cut off from the man and beast = that falsity will destroy all the intelligence of truth and affection of good in the natural man. AE 724:28.
Without conjunction with Heaven, and through it with the Lord, man would not be man, but a beast.
Slain the names of men seven thousand () = that all the truths of good perished...
Man = intelligence; thus, also, the understanding of truth.
Man = the spiritual affection of truth; beast, the natural affection of good.
This would never have been said unless there were something given to man from which he is able to do what is good; and that which has been given him appears to him as his own, although it is not his.

By man, who was called Adam and Eve, is meant that Church; for it is said male and female created He them, and called their name man... Taken together, and conjoined in marriage, they are called man... The reason these two things, doctrine and life, taken together, and as it were conjoined in marriage, are called man, and also make the Church, is that man is man from the understanding of truth and the will of good; consequently from the doctrine of life... and the life of doctrine...
For all truth from the Lord is in its form a man. Hence the Angels... are human forms...

As man is formed, so is he perfected in intelligence and wisdom, and becomes a man; for no man is a man from his natural mind but he becomes man through intelligence and wisdom from the Lord; and in proportion as he is intelligent and wise, in the same proportion he is a beautiful man and an Angel of Heaven. (Otherwise) he is a monster and not a man... From these things it may be evident that man is not man from his parents, but from the Lord, from whom he is born anew.

The difference between animals and men is that animals cannot think and speak truths, and will and do goods, from God; but that men can, and thus believe the things which they think, and love the things which they will; and this as of themselves...
Before men () = before those especially who are in the conceit of Own intelligence...
There is also the lowest degree, which is corporeal and material, and which is with man...
The Angels (of the Ultimate Heaven), being as to understanding almost like men in the world...

This arcanum: That each and all things of man, both of his mind and of his body, are forms of love in a wonderful series; and the organs of the brain and face, and also the members and viscera of the body, are perpetual contextures which correspond to the affections of Heaven...
Man is his own truth, or falsity, not only as to the thoughts which are from his will, but also as to his universal body...
(The consorts) then appear as one man.

To descend from heaven upon men () = from Hell destroying the understanding of truth with those who are of the Church; for by men are signified the men of the Church as to the understanding of truth; or, what is the same, the understanding of truth which is with the men of the Church.
For man in the world is in his fulness; and therefore he can be conceived and born there; and afterwards be imbued with knowledge, intelligence, and wisdom...
(Thus) God is now more a man than the Angels.
The reason the Lord is the Only Man, is...
These forms are men...
God is a perfect man, with a face like a man, and with a body like a man. There is no difference as to form; but as to essence...

That all things are from Life itself... which is a man, may be illustrated by the man who has been created, in that as to his ultimates, his mediates, and his inmosts, he is a man. For the man who in the world... has been corporeal, thus stupid, after (death) appears as a man: the man who in the world... has been sensuous or natural... after death appears as a man: the man who in the world has been rational... after death... appears as a man: the man who in the world has been spiritual... after death appears as a man perfect according to the reception of life from the Lord: the man with whom the third degree of life has been opened... after death... appears as a man in all perfection. The life itself with him is a man, whether sensuous and natural, rational, spiritual, or celestial... the man in whom they are is only a recipient.

As it is in the least types, so is it in the greatest. The universal angelic Heaven in the whole complex is a man: each Heaven by itself, the First, the ISecond, and the Third, is a man: each Society of the Heavens, greater or less, is a man: nay, the Church on earth in general is a man: all collective bodies, which are called Churches, are, by themselves, men. It is said the Church, and there are meant all with whom the Church is, in the complex. So does the Church on earth appear to the Angels... The reason of this appearance is that the life which is from the Lord is a man. The life from the Lord is love and wisdom; hence such as is the reception of love and wisdom from the Lord, such is the man. These things testify... that all things have been created from the life which is God and which is a man.
Without this perception (as if life were in him) man would not be man. Explained.
Man is a recipient subject...
(This) is not from man, but from the Lord... (This) is not from man, but from Hell. Explained.
That man is only a recipient of good and truth from the Lord, and of evil and falsity from Hell...

The life which makes man to be man, and to be distinguished from brute animals... is perpetually from the Lord with him; but the derivative understanding and will of man... are changed and varied according to the reception... AE 1162:end.
The order into which man has been created, is to love the Lord above all things, and his neighbour as himself...
That all things may return to the First... which takes place through man.
It has been given to see a Society consisting of thousands of Angels as one man of medium stature...

I have not seen, but have heard that the Church on earth is before the Lord as one man; and also that it is distinguished into Societies, and that each Society is a man; and also that all who are within this man are within Heaven; but that those who are outside of it are in Hell...

The reason that Heaven and the Church are a man in the concrete, or the greatest, less, and least complex, is that God is a man, and thence the proceeding Divine... is the like in every least and greatest, which is a man... AE 1223:end.
(So also Hell) before the Lord is as one man, but as a devil man, or monster man...
Spirits do not see the man; but only his affections.
Thus also a society on earth appears before the Angels in the Heavens as one man.
Each kingdom is presented before the Angels in Heaven as one man when the Lord pleases...
That at this day for man to be man he must be charity in form. General article. Char 126.
From the Divine Itself in itself man cannot be created; for thus he would be the Divine in itself; but he can be formed from created and finite things, in which the Divine can be...
That in such a form is man in particular. General article.
(Thus) man is the complex of all uses... DLove 8:2.
That in such a form is man in general. General article.
That in proportion as man is in the love of use, in the same proportion he is in the Lord's love, in the same proportion be loves him, and loves the neighbour, and is man. General article.
For every use which is in any way of service to the general good... is a man. Explained.
Nay, the parts of parts... are men more than the compounded [parts]; because all perfection increases towards the interiors...

That every degree, even the least in man, is a man from its use... falls into a spiritual idea; for in a spiritual idea man is not a person, but a use; for a spiritual idea is devoid of the idea of person... and therefore when one sees another in Heaven, he does indeed see him as a man, but he thinks of him as a use... Thus every good use is in form a man.
That those are not men... who love themselves above all things, and the world as themselves. General article.
That every man is an affection; and that there are as many various affections as there are men born, or who will be born to eternity. General article.
